newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end down on weather, cash.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end down on weather, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Monday in a lackluster session, undermined by forecasts for milder weather this week that pressured the cash, industry sources said.
November slipped 4.7 cents to close at $2.30 per million British thermal units. December settled 5.2 cents lower at $2.48, while deferreds ended down by 0.6 to 2.5 cents.
"With the utility side out today (for Columbus Day holiday), you had more sellers than buyers, and with no weather, I think we'll be on the defensive for a while," said one Texas-based trader.
With little extreme heat or cold on the horizon this week, few expected a significant rally in cash or futures near-term.
Technically, many still expected more downside despite the November close at $2.30. They pegged next support in the mid-teens, with resistance seen at $2.40 and then at the recent high of $2.59.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices slipped more than five cents Monday to the mid-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were off several cents to the $2.05-2.10 area. New York city gate gas fell a few cents Monday to the mid-$2.60s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 0.4 cent to $2.172. NYMEX said 28,738 Hub contracts traded, down slightly from Friday's revised tally of 29,746.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled one cent lower at $1.04, while deferreds closed down by ont-half to two cents. NYMEX said six Alberta contracts traded, down sharply from Friday's total of 174.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished down two cents at $2.035, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said five Permian lots changed hands compared to 50 on Friday.
On the KCBT, November settled four cents lower at $2.06, while deferreds ended down by one to 3.2 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.7 cent to 24.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
